title: P1 — Port-range allocator leak: non-force destroy returns not_found after userdel failure WITHOUT freeing the range; TTL-expired agents exhausted the whole las-03 pool (proven 2026-09-03)
detail: PROVEN LIVE on bunker-las-03 (imhotep foreman tick T230, 2026-09-03 ~19:45Z): after the fleet-wide 17:11Z bunkerd restart, audit export shows 19 successful SpawnAgent vs 9 ok DestroyAgent + 15 not_found DestroyAgent → 19−9 = 10 = the ENTIRE pool (config port_range 30000-31000, 100/agent) held by agent IDs invisible to the registry. ListAgents = 0 agents while SpawnAgent failed 26x with 'port range allocation: no free port ranges available (pool exhausted: 10 ranges)' from 18:15Z to 19:48Z (QA spawn bursts 19:10-19:19Z + retries). Host also shows 48 bunker-* users persisting (many with RUNNING rootless dockerd processes) while the registry lists none. ROOT CAUSE CHAIN: internal/agent/manager_destroy.go Step 3 (~:63-73) — non-force destroy where userdel -rf fails (agent user still owns running processes: rootless dockerd/rootlesskit daemons) does m.tracker.Unregister(agentID) and returns Status not_found WITHOUT calling m.portAlloc.Free(agentID); Free only runs at ~:115 after full cleanup. The TTL reaper (manager.go reapExpiredAgents, 1-min ticker → Destroy non-force) is a frequent triggering caller: expired agent whose rootless dockerd didn't die in time → userdel fails → registry slot freed, port range leaked forever (allocator is in-memory; restart clears it, orphan users/daemons do NOT clear). Secondary defect: Step 1 dockerd stop (stopDockerdDirect + systemctl --user fallback) never WAITS for the rootlesskit/dockerd PIDs to actually exit before userdel -rf runs. FIX SKETCH: (1) call m.portAlloc.Free(agentID) in the not_found early-return path — unconditional, idempotent (Free no-ops for unknown IDs); (2) harden Step 1: after stop, poll up to ~10s for the agent user's rootlesskit/dockerd PIDs to exit, SIGKILL stragglers, then userdel; (3) same Free-before-return guarantee on any other early return between Allocate and the final Free. PASS: (1) unit test — non-force destroy with failing userdel returns not_found AND portAlloc.Available() is back to full; (2) unit test — force-mode destroy with failing userdel still frees; (3) TTL-reaper path covered — expired agent with a running process does not leak a range; (4) existing suite green; VERIFY-PASS evidence committed. OPS NOTE (not part of PASS): after fix deploys, las-03 needs a steward/Bane root pass to restart bunkerd (reclaims the 10 leaked ranges — sudo restart is approval-blocked in cron sessions) and to clean the 48 orphan bunker-* users + their dockerd daemons. Detection recipe for recurrence: bunker audit export → compare ok-spawn count vs ok-destroy count since last restart; delta > 0 = leaked ranges.

title: [P1] bunker-qa.sh spawn_agent retry loop leaks the attempt-1 agent when attempt 1 spawns server-side but returns unparseable output — run destroyed a different agent ID than it spawned; cleanup() also swallows destroy failures with || true
detail: LIVE 2026-09-15 (dogfood REAL tick targeting bunker, server bunker-las-02, run /tmp/dagger-role-qa-2259038-1789510605536506949): run.log cleanup line says 'destroying temp agent 0ecbb9e8', but `bunker list --server bunker-las-02` after the run showed agent 230abb5b STILL RUNNING with creation timestamp inside the run's spawn window (2026-09-15T15:18:54-07:00). Mechanism: spawn_agent() (bunker-qa.sh:32-45) loops 3x on `bunker spawn` output parsing (`grep -oP 'keys/\K[a-f0-9]+'`); a spawn that SUCCEEDS server-side (agent user created) but whose output fails to parse (CLI warning/mixed output) makes attempt 2 spawn a SECOND agent while the first is orphaned — BUNKER_QA_AGENT is set only after the loop succeeds, so cleanup() (bunker-qa.sh:384) destroys only the last agent; the TTL is the only backstop for the leak. Secondary: cleanup() pipes `bunker destroy ... || true`, so a failed destroy is never surfaced (destroy-failure escalation contract from the bunker-agent-isolation skill is defeated). Found and destroyed manually same day (`bunker destroy 230abb5b` rc=0, server back to 1 agent). Fix direction: (a) capture ALL ids parsed across spawn attempts and destroy non-selected ones before proceeding, or fail the run; (b) log + emit a FAIL/INFO evidence cell when `bunker destroy` exits non-zero instead of || true; (c) optional post-destroy verify: re-list and assert the id is gone.

reasoning.note: Filed by the 2026-09-15 dogfood run; evidence is the run's own log line vs the post-run bunker list (both quoted in detail). Agent destroyed by the runner before filing — no orphan left behind.

review_notes: Frequency estimate: only fires when spawn attempt N succeeds server-side but parses empty — rare, but each leak holds a full agent slot (64G disk pool) until TTL expiry and can push the pool toward the capacity preflight limit (QA-OFF-BY-ONE-9 class).
foreman_note: QA foreman 2026-09-18 (qa-foreman-2026-09-18): live mechanism + numbers for this leak, measured on bunker-las-03 across two consecutive spawn attempts (daemon journal 04:46:30-04:48:11 PDT; this cycle's own launch attempts). The leak is NOT only the retry-loop case — the ROLLBACK ITSELF fails, because userdel runs on the already-cancelled spawn context: `WARN rolling back: removing user username=bunker-<id>` immediately followed by `ERROR rollback userdel failed agent_id=<id> error="context canceled" output=""` on all 3 attempts. Cancellation root cause: the rootless-docker install downloads Docker 29.8.1 static 82.0M + 11.4M at ~1.5-2.3 MB/s (~50-60s); the attempt that got furthest died at `systemd-run rootless dockerd failed: context canceled` while dockerd was already UP (`dockerd exited after SIGTERM`), i.e. the deadline fired during/just after a successful install. Host state now: 11 `bunker-*` users, 0 registered agents, 2.5G of /home (10 x 247M + 36K), port ranges 30000-30099 and 30100-30199 for an 8-agent pool ceiling. Durable fix needs both (a) a rollback on a fresh/independent context or a startup orphan-sweeper, and (b) a longer spawn deadline or a pre-provisioned/cached rootless installer, since the download alone consumes ~50-60s of the deadline budget. Cross-refs: INT-CI-020 (rollback-under-cancelled-context test premise), DF-BUNKER-24 (orphan keys), GAP-080 (orphan dirs), DF-BUNKER-10 (daemon version drift).

title: [P1] CI RED on HEAD b9c7840 — build-and-test / Unit tests failed: internal/audit TestShipFailureRetriesThenReplays asserts a ship-state invariant the code does not guarantee (in-memory queue drained but the persisted shipstate still reads ok/queue_depth 1)
detail: EVIDENCE (live, this tick): run 35066829049 (headSha b9c7840 = tick 427's board commit, created 2026-09-16T07:05:58Z) conclusion=failure; job-level expansion `gh run view 35066829049 --json jobs` -> build-and-test FAILED at step `Unit tests`, other three jobs (gitreins-guard, root-suite, regression) skipped. Failing step log: '--- FAIL: TestShipFailureRetriesThenReplays (0.32s) ship_test.go:280: ship state = &{ShipTo:http://127.0.0.1:38697 LastAttempt:2026-09-16T07:06:42Z LastResult:ok LastSuccess:2026-09-16T07:06:42Z QueueDepth:1}, want ok/0 after replay'. NOT a deterministic break: the same test passes locally (go test -count=30 -short ./internal/audit/ -run TestShipFailureRetriesThenReplays => ok 9.1s) and the previous push run 35065380890 (48a2f5b) was 4/4 job-level green, so this is a CI-only flake that hides a real consistency window. MECHANISM (code-traced in internal/audit/ship.go): run() pops the drained item and computes depth=len(s.queue) while holding s.mu, then RELEASES the lock and only afterwards calls writeState() (ship.go:366-368) — the persisted shipstate therefore still carries the PREVIOUS attempt's snapshot (ok/queue_depth 1) at the instant a reader observes the drained in-memory snapshot; ship_test.go's drain loop breaks on the in-memory snapshot() and then reads the state FILE once, with no convergence deadline, so the file assertion (line ~280) races the state write. TWO independent inconsistencies in the same surface: (a) the segment-read-failure path calls recordResult(fmt.Sprintf(\"error: read segment: %v\", err), 0) with a HARDCODED depth 0 (ship.go:276), so the persisted queue_depth can contradict the live queue; (b) state writes happen from two goroutines (the run loop and recordResult on the Log()/rotation path) with no ordering guard, so an older attempt's snapshot can overwrite a newer one. IMPACT: `bunker audit status` can report a queue depth / last_result that never corresponded to the real queue at any observable moment; CI is red on HEAD, which blocks the whole lane. FIX DIRECTION: publish the state file from the same critical section that publishes the queue depth (or serialize state writes and derive depth from the live queue instead of a caller-supplied value), then make the test assert FILE convergence with a bounded deadline instead of a single read after an in-memory drain. PASS: (1) no caller passes a depth that disagrees with len(queue) at write time; (2) a deterministic regression test fails on pre-fix code and passes post-fix; (3) go test -count=1 -short ./... green; (4) go test -count=20 -short ./internal/audit/ -race green; (5) next push run for the fix commit is job-level 4/4 green.
reasoning: CI is red on HEAD for a test that CI-only flakes: the flake masks a real shipstate/critical-section ordering defect, so the fix is in-repo code + test, not a rerun.

title: [P1] bunker exec rejects --server before the agent-id and drops --timeout there too — global flag grammar inconsistent with every other command, error misleads
detail: Live at HEAD-built CLI (66d4150): `bunker --server bunker-las-04 exec df0916a -- sh -c 'whoami'` → `bunker: stream error: not_found: agent "--server" not found` (exec's DisableFlagParsing peeler only scans flags AFTER args[0], so the global position that spawn/status/list/info/audit all accept becomes the agent-id). title: [P1] README promises 'Private /tmp per agent' but a v0.1.3 daemon silently gives exec sessions the HOST /tmp — feature availability is invisible to the user
detail: Reproduced on live fleet daemon bunker-las-04 (v0.1.3): `bunker exec <id> -- ls /tmp` returns the HOST's /tmp (host systemd-private dirs of colord/fwupd/polkit/switcheroo visible to the agent) and /srv/bunker-share does not exist — while README (current HEAD) states every agent gets an enforced private /tmp via pam_namespace with fail-closed validation, and /srv/bunker-share is the sanctioned exchange dir. Root cause is version gating, not a code defect: the isolation feature (GAP-075, commit 9703082) is in NO release tag (git tag --contains 9703082 = empty; v0.1.4 tag predates it), and no command surfaces which isolation level a daemon provides — `bunker info` shows limits but nothing about /tmp policy. A user on any tagged release gets host-shared /tmp while reading docs that promise isolation. FIX (either side): cut a release containing 9703082 so tagged daemons match the README; AND make the daemon advertise capability/isolation level (ServerInfo field) with `bunker status`/`info` printing it, so silent downgrades become visible.

title: [P2] bunker mount fails reproducibly against a healthy agent with raw 'read: Connection reset by peer' — no retry, no actionable error
detail: On bunker-las-04 with agent df0916a (running, exec + docker + tunnel all healthy): `bunker mount df0916a /mnt` failed 2/2 times with `read: Connection reset by peer` + `bunker: sshfs failed: exit status 1`. Raw `ssh` to the agent works; the sftp subsystem answers (ssh -s sftp returns protocol banner); plain `sshfs` from the control host failed identically to the CLI, once in verbose mode showing auth success then 'remote host has disconnected' — consistent with sshd rate/parallel-session limiting (MaxStartups) on the many-connection agent host, where each sshfs attempt opens a fresh connection while existing tunnels/sessions are alive. FIX: add bounded retry with backoff to the mount command's sshfs invocation, and wrap the failure with 'sshfs connection reset — agent host may be limiting parallel SSH sessions; try again or close other tunnels'.

title: [P1] destroy never disables systemd linger — every agent ever spawned leaves a /var/lib/systemd/linger entry forever (8,024 accumulated on the demo/CI host vs 2 live users); measured effect: the same spawn went 29.8s deadline_exceeded → 17.0s success after pruning

title: [P1] Every bunker-* SSH session on the demo host is DENIED (pam_open_session: System error) — exec/mount/cp are all broken against healthy, running agents; the provisioned GAP-075 PAM block demands a group membership the stale deployed daemon never grants
detail: LIVE (foreman tick 439, bunker-mvp, agent foreman-vrf-1789573645 — spawned and registered as RUNNING by the deployed daemon). SYMPTOM: ssh to the agent returns exit status 254 with the login banner as the only output and NO command output; sshfs reports 'remote host has disconnected' / 'read: Connection reset by peer'. sshd journal per connection: 'pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user bunker-<id>(uid=1010)' then 'error: PAM: pam_open_session(): System error'. The daemon's flagship workflow (exec over SSH, mount, cp) therefore cannot work on the demo host at all while the daemon reports the agent running. ROOT CAUSE, ONE COMMAND: /etc/pam.d/sshd carries the GAP-075 block — classifier `pam_succeed_if user !~ bunker-*`, then `[success=ignore default=die] pam_exec.so quiet /usr/lib/bunker/pam-tmp-guard verify bunker-agents`, then `required pam_namespace.so`. `PAM_USER=<fresh agent> /usr/lib/bunker/pam-tmp-guard verify bunker-agents` → 'bunker-pam-guard: user <id> is not a member of bunker-agents', rc=1 → pam_exec maps non-zero to PAM_SYSTEM_ERR → `default=die` denies the session. An OLDER agent that is in the group passes (PAM_USER=bunker-imgspec-none → rc=0) and its SSH works, so the discriminator is GROUP MEMBERSHIP, not agent health. Host has the SSH-side provision (drop-in + helper dated 2026-09-13) while /opt/bunker/bunkerd is the 2026-08-30 build that predates the spawn-side 'isolation-provision' stage that adds new agents to bunker-agents — host provisioned, daemon too old = every agent that daemon spawns is locked out of SSH. FIX: (1) restore congruence — deploy the HEAD daemon to the demo so spawn grants the membership (this is the DF-BUNKER-10 lag class and it must happen before ANY live exec/mount verification on the demo can be trusted); or `bunker host-provision --uninstall --apply` to return to shared /tmp — never hand-delete only the drop-in, whose own comment warns that the remaining pam_exec precondition then fails closed and locks EVERY bunker-* session out; (2) make the skew impossible — host-provision refuses (or loudly warns) when the installed daemon is older than the hardening it installs, and spawn grants the membership BEFORE the agent is reported ready; (3) operator-facing — `bunker exec` surfaces the session-denial cause instead of a bare exit 254. PASS: (1) a freshly spawned agent on the demo host accepts `bunker exec <id> -- whoami` with real output (no 254) and `bunker mount <id>` succeeds; (2) a test proves the provision/daemon version-skew check rejects an older daemon; (3) spawn reports ready only after an SSH exec probe succeeds. RELATED / REFUTES: DF-BUNKER-14 (mount fails against a healthy agent) blames the CLI's fixed `-o allow_other`; that is REFUTED live — sshfs with allow_other AND without it fail identically against the same agent, the raw SFTP channel is clean (.hushlogin changes nothing), and a plain `ssh` to that agent already fails with 254.

reasoning.note: Found while verifying DF-BUNKER-14's premise live. The chain a later tick must not re-derive: the sshd PAM journal line, the one-command guard reproduction, and the membership discriminator between a locked-out fresh agent and a working older one. Filed separately from DF-BUNKER-14 so the mount row closes against the right root cause instead of an allow_other fallback that fixes nothing.

Run 35142150138 (sha 7321f2c) is the first completed run whose tree CONTAINS the INT-CI-008 fix bb751f5, and it is red at job level twice: (a) root-suite job step 'Root-gated suite (TestSpawn|TestCgroup|TestConcurrency)' FAILURE — TestSpawn_WithProvidedAgentID, _GeneratesSSHKeys, _PersistsSSHKey, _DiskMaxBytesEnforced, _TmpDirExists, _AuthorizedKeysHasEnvironment, _SystemdUnitHasUlimits all fail; (b) regression job step 'E2E battery' FAILURE — PASS 31 / FAIL 2 with the battery's own spawn red ('✗ spawn agent — Creating agent...'), CERTIFIED BINARY MATCH (commit reported 7321f2c). (17 occurrences in the run log), preceded in the daemon log by 'agent user manager unreachable; transient unit disable skipped ... reason=no user session bus ... Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'. MECHANISM (as far as the evidence goes, do not overclaim): the rootless installer writes ~/.config/systemd/user/docker.service and immediately runs `systemctl --user start docker.service`; when the agent's user manager is not up/reachable at that moment the unit is unknown to it. FIX DIRECTION: (1) make the rootless-install stage prove the agent's user manager is reachable (and start it / reset-failed + retry once) BEFORE running the installer, and make the installer's `systemctl --user start` retry after a daemon-reload, so a freshly written unit is never 'not found'; (2) if the evidence shows the two jobs contend, serialize the CI jobs that spawn agents on the shared host (or give the battery and the root-suite disjoint spawn budget) instead of running them concurrently. title: [P1] Spawn reports an agent ready without proving its SSH session works - implement the bounded SSH exec probe (the remaining conjunct of INT-DEMO-001 criterion 3)
detail: Filed by tick 447 out of the Tier 2 judge verdict f3209ad3 on INT-DEMO-001-C3, which found this conjunct of criterion 3 unmet: no SSH exec probe exists anywhere in the spawn path (grep for BatchMode/ConnectTimeout/ssh-echo/ssh-true = 0 hits), manager_spawn.go runs user-create -> isolation -> keygen -> authorized-keys -> rootless-install -> dockerd-start -> container-cap -> image-build -> slice-limits -> register and sets rec.Status="running" at manager_spawn.go:571 with no session probe against the agent user. Why it matters: the 2026-09-16 demo outage (INT-DEMO-001) had the daemon reporting a RUNNING agent while every SSH session was denied by PAM (pam_open_session: System error, ssh exit 254) - a user of that agent could not exec, mount or cp, and nothing in the spawn result said so. Required design: after authorized_keys/dockerd are in place and BEFORE the agent is reported ready, run a bounded SSH exec probe as the agent user (bunker-<id>@localhost with rec.SshPrivateKeyPath, the same target/options as the exec path, e.g. `whoami`): hard timeout ~10s, at most 2-3 tries with a short backoff, never unbounded; probe OK -> spawn returns as today (log the probe result); probe FAILED -> do NOT report ready, reuse the existing fail() rollback and return an error naming the cause, reusing internal/server/exec_session.go's classification when the signature matches. PASS: (a) a unit test proves spawn does not report ready when the probe fails and that the happy path still returns a normal spawn response (inject/fake the probe - no live ssh in unit tests); (b) the happy path is unchanged live (spawn+exec on the demo host); (c) live E2E battery VERIFY-PASS on bunker-mvp (AGENTS.md gate 3 - spawn behaviour), which also depends on INT-CI-010.
reasoning: The remaining conjunct of INT-DEMO-001 criterion 3 (Tier 2 verdict f3209ad3 found the spawn path never proved the session): closing it removes the exact lie the 2026-09-16 demo outage produced - a RUNNING agent whose every SSH session was PAM-denied.

title: [P1] Standalone E2E gate takes over the live daemon and ports (nested regression suite pkills bunkerd, rebinds :18080/:19090 and deletes the operator CLI config) and its section-12 nested verdict is vacuous
detail: [P1] Standalone E2E gate cannot reach VERIFY-PASS on a host with a systemd-managed daemon: the nested regression suite takes over the live ports (pkill bunkerd + its own daemon on :18080/:19090) and DELETES the operator CLI config, and section 12's nested verdict is vacuous. MEASURED (foreman tick 450, bunker-mvp, HEAD 1872d22, /usr/local/bin binaries certified MATCH): `BUNKER_TOKEN=<daemon token> BUNKER_DAEMON_URL=http://localhost:18080 BUNKERD_REST_ADDR=:18080 BUNKERD_GRPC_ADDR=:19090 bash e2e-full-battery.sh` -> Pass 111 / Fail 4 -> VERIFY-FAIL. Red cells: (1) section 13 'allowed spec spawn failed - Creating agent... bunker: spawn agent: unavailable: dial tcp [::1]:18080: connect: connection refused'; (2) section 13 'jq NOT found in agent image - agent "e2e-imgspec" not found' (cascade of 1); (3) section 14 'destroy of a never-seen ID unexpectedly succeeded'; (4) 'OPERATOR CLI CONFIG MODIFIED BY THIS RUN - /root/.bunker/config.yaml before sha256:f4098a0b3d594434... after ABSENT'. Host journal at the same minute: bunkerd[2139762] shutting down signal=terminated 13:43:17Z -> systemd 'Started bunkerd.service' 13:43:24 -> 'bunkerd: server error: listen tcp :18080: bind: address already in use' 13:43:25 -> started again 13:43:27 (systemctl show bunkerd -p NRestarts -> 4). Linger 73 -> 74 (one stale entry left by the run; pruned afterwards with the deployed `bunker linger prune`, kept 1 live). MECHANISM (two independent harness defects, standalone path only): (A) TAKEOVER COLLISION - e2e-full-battery.sh section 12 invokes the nested suite in standalone mode WITHOUT dedicated ports (the else branch ~line 1351), so regression-tests.sh inherits the battery's exported BUNKERD_REST_ADDR=:18080 / BUNKERD_GRPC_ADDR=:19090, runs `pkill bunkerd` (line 111; again at cleanup line 91), starts its OWN daemon on those production ports with a temp auth-disabled config (line 156), and line 122 does `rm -rf /root/.bunker /run/bunker/* /etc/bunkerd/ssh/*` - i.e. it destroys exactly the operator CLI state that INT-CI-010's isolation work exists to protect. The systemd unit auto-restarts and races the nested daemon for :18080, so the production daemon is unavailable exactly when sections 13/14 dial it. (B) VACUOUS NESTED VERDICT - `REG_EXIT=$?` (~line 1353) reads the status of the surrounding if-block and the command substitution ends with `|| true`, so REG_EXIT is ALWAYS 0: the battery asserts 'regression suite PASSED' even though the nested suite printed 'PASS: 16 / FAIL: 14'. REG_PASS/REG_FAIL are naive `grep -c PASS/FAIL` counts of the transcript words, not the nested suite's tally. A nested suite that dies is therefore invisible. FIX DIRECTION: (1) give the nested suite its own isolated ports in standalone mode (coexist already uses :29092/:28082) and make regression-tests.sh refuse to `pkill bunkerd` when a systemd-managed production daemon is active, stopping only the daemon it started itself; (2) never `rm -rf` operator CLI state - run the nested suite with its own BUNKER_HOME/HOME and remove only that throwaway dir, gating the /run/bunker + /etc/bunkerd/ssh sweeps on daemon ownership; (3) capture the nested exit status without `|| true` masking it and FAIL the battery (not `note`) on a non-zero nested exit, counting the nested suite's own tally lines; (4) sections 13/14 must probe daemon reachability and name the endpoint before cascading 'not found' cells; (5) README states the standalone contract. PASS: (a) --self-test PASS incl. new assertions (nested suite gets non-production ports in standalone; a nested suite exiting 1 flips section 12 to a failure; the battery never removes a config it did not create); (b) grep-provable: no unconditional `pkill bunkerd` reachable while a systemd-managed daemon is active, no `rm -rf` of the operator config dir; (c) --show-plan/--bin-report unchanged; (d) live standalone gate on bunker-mvp prints 0 FAIL / VERIFY-PASS with the production daemon uptime continuous (NRestarts unchanged) and /root/.bunker/config.yaml's sha256 unchanged; (e) coexist path unchanged (CI stays green).
reasoning: Found by executing INT-CI-011's standalone-gate criterion live on the demo host: the run was FOUR cells from green and every red cell traces to the nested suite's take-over, which is a harness defect rather than a product defect. The vacuous section-12 verdict is filed in the same row because it is the reason this class stayed invisible in earlier runs (the battery reported 'regression suite PASSED' with 14 nested failures).

title: [P1] spawn fails at rootless-install when the allocated uid is recycled (previous owner's user@<uid> manager still active -> session-bus daemon-reload fails) and the failed-spawn rollback leaks the linger entry
detail: [P1] spawn dies at stage rootless-install whenever the freshly allocated uid was RECYCLED from an agent whose systemd user manager is still live, and the failed-spawn rollback leaks the linger entry. MEASURED (foreman tick 450, bunker-mvp, HEAD 1872d22, deployed daemon 0.1.4/1872d22): the standalone E2E gate's nested regression suite ran 14 red cells, ALL cascade from one spawn. The daemon's own attribution (/var/log/bunkerd-regression.log): 'spawn entering stage regr-alpha stage=rootless-install' -> WARN 'agent user manager unreachable from the agent session before the rootless install' user=bunker-regr-alpha unit=user@1002.service state='unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success)' linger_entries=3 -> WARN 'userdel failed; terminating user processes and retrying' error='userdel bunker-regr-alpha: exit status 8 (output: userdel: user bunker-regr-alpha is currently used by process 2168325)' -> ERROR 'spawn failed stage=rootless-install error=... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success); linger entries: 3'. uid 1002 had been used minutes earlier by a destroyed agent in the same gate run (foreman-idemo-*), and systemctl showed user@1002.service still ACTIVE at spawn time (it only went 'failed (Result: signal)' when the rollback killed it). SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME PATH: the rollback of a failed spawn does NOT un-linger - after the run /var/lib/systemd/linger held bunker-regr-alpha, bunker-1dd412d0 and bunker-ff86d69a while none of those users existed (the destroy path DOES un-linger, proven tick 441; the failed-spawn rollback path apparently does not). All three were pruned with the deployed `bunker linger prune` (scanned 4, stale removed 3, kept 1 live). WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the pre-INT-CI-012 harness printed 'regression suite PASSED' over the nested suite's 'PASS: 16 / FAIL: 14' (see INT-CI-012). FIX DIRECTION: (1) in the rootless-install stage, treat an ACTIVE user manager for the allocated uid as a live signal, not a failure: the reachability probe's `systemctl --user daemon-reload` must not fail the spawn when user@<uid>.service is active for a DIFFERENT (recycled) user name - either assert the runtime dir/bus belongs to the agent's own user before probing, or retry after resetting the stale manager for that uid; (2) never allocate a uid whose user manager is still active (or stop/terminate it as part of spawn's fresh-uid preparation); (3) make the failed-spawn rollback un-linger exactly like destroy does. PASS: (a) a test proves spawn succeeds (or fails with an attribution naming the recycled uid) when the allocated uid's previous user manager is still active; (b) a live repro on the demo host: spawn an agent, destroy it, immediately spawn again (uid recycled) -> spawn completes; (c) `ls /var/lib/systemd/linger` is unchanged across a FAILED spawn (rollback un-lingers); (d) the nested regression suite's 14 spawn/exec/list cells go green in the standalone gate.
reasoning: Surfaced by the live standalone gate AFTER INT-CI-012's harness fix restored an honest nested verdict: the 14 red cells were previously reported as 'regression suite PASSED'. The attribution comes from the daemon's own breadcrumb (stage + unit state + userdel conflict + linger count), not from a guess, and the uid was demonstrably recycled inside one gate run.

title: [P3] Section 14 'destroy of a never-seen ID' is red in the standalone gate: the CLI returned 0 for an ID absent from the durable registry while the daemon provably answers 404 not_found
detail: [P3] e2e-full-battery.sh section 14 'destroy of a never-seen ID still reports not_found' is red on a host where the battery runs repeatedly. EVIDENCE (foreman tick 450, standalone gate on bunker-mvp, 113 PASS / 2 FAIL): the cell `bcli destroy gap070-never-seen` (NON-force) exited 0, so the battery reported 'destroy of a never-seen ID unexpectedly succeeded', while the preceding cell 'repeated destroy of a known absent agent succeeds (first=0 second=0)' passed. DISCRIMINATOR CHECKED: the ID is NOT in the durable registry (`grep -c gap070-never-seen /var/lib/bunkerd/agents.jsonl` = 0), so the known-absent path is not the explanation. An INDEPENDENT observation on the same host in the same hour: a throwaway daemon (nested regression suite) answered DestroyAgent for the ID 'nonexistent' with 404 and logged 'destroy agent failed: agent "nonexistent" not found', i.e. the DAEMON does distinguish never-seen IDs. The red is therefore most likely in the CLI/exit-code mapping used by the battery's bcli wrapper (or in the --force/no-force flag handling) rather than in the daemon. FIX DIRECTION: one probe to localise - run the same non-force destroy against a daemon with an empty registry (coexist battery daemon) and compare `bcli destroy gap070-never-seen; echo $?` with a raw gRPC/REST DestroyAgent call; use a per-run unique ID so a previous run's known-index cannot make the cell ambiguous. PASS: the cell is either proven green with a never-seen ID on a clean daemon (and the harness records which daemon the destroy hit) or the real not_found mapping bug is filed with the failing seam named.
reasoning: Filed because it is one of the two remaining red cells of the live standalone gate and the row that owned the gate (INT-CI-012) is harness-scoped; a red cell with no owner rots. The evidence separates the daemon (correct 404) from the caller (exit 0), which is what makes it a cheap next probe instead of a re-investigation.

title: [P2] Tier 2 eval input-cap starvation RECURS on this repo (2M -> 4M -> 8M -> 16M, one rung per tick): the evaluator re-sends the whole repo every iteration, so the cumulative budget dies before any merit judgment
detail: INT-SPAWN-001's Tier 2 returned INCOMPLETE with 'Eval cap exceeded: Input token budget (8.0M) exceeded (8.0M used)' (verdict 73e7ecae) exactly like GAP-068 (2M, tick 429), GAP-077 (2M, earlier) and the sibling cap-starvation cases; each fix has been another rung (2M -> 4M ef429dc, 4M -> 8M tick 450, 8M -> 16M commit 25a43d2 tick 451). A cap-starved run is NOT a merit verdict and it still flips .gitreins/tasks.yaml to complete, so the real risk is silent acceptance of an unevaluated commit. FIX DIRECTION (durable, not another rung): measure what actually fills the budget - the evaluator runs with file_scope: full, so every iteration re-sends the repo context; options are (a) file_scope: changed for this repo (with the caveat that a committed, clean tree hides the diff - see the pre-solve answer 1540), (b) raising compaction_threshold sensitivity / lowering code_context_budget from 0.40, or (c) splitting a heavy criterion into grep-able sub-criteria (pre-solve 1486). PASS: (1) a measured breakdown of where the 16M goes in one Tier 2 run on this repo (iterations x tokens/iteration, with the real numbers); (2) one concrete config/criteria change justified by that measurement, not by escalation; (3) two consecutive Tier 2 runs on this repo finish with a PASS/FAIL merit verdict without hitting any cap.
reasoning: This is the third tick in a row where a Tier 2 verdict on bunker was a cap artifact rather than a judgment, and each 'fix' has been a bigger number. Escalation is not a fix: it defers the same starvation into a more expensive failure and hides real merit failures behind INCOMPLETE. || TICK 459 CLOSURE - picked as the highest-value non-blocked in-repo row (GAP-067 blocked; the 30+ QA-BUNKER rows are QA-machinery findings - bunker-qa.sh lives in ~/.hermes/scripts, not this repo; tick 458 deferred this row as 'a measurement pass over a 16M-token eval'). Pre-solve corpus was consulted first (class gitreins-tier2-input-token-cap-exceeded -> answers 1540/1516/1486): every recorded answer is another cap rung, which is exactly what this row forbids, so the tick measured instead. MEASURED DRIVER: the counter is quadratic in iterations because the whole conversation is re-sent every call. Pre-change instrumented run 616c1d33 (INT-CI-017, HEAD 848625c): 23 calls, prompt 6,211->29,323 tokens, least-squares P0=5,435 + 1,119/iteration, cumulative 408,009 (2.55% of cap), 0 compactions, 0 cap lines. S(165)=16.0M vs max_iterations=200 => the cap dies before the iteration budget can be spent; and compaction - the only caller of eval_cap.reset_context_tracking - was dead because 0.90 x 16M = 14.4M was 491x the largest single prompt ever measured. FIX: make the engine-read knobs live, scope the judge to the whole repo (file_scope: full; with `changed` + a clean tree the allowed set was 6 bookkeeping files and the judged artifact was rejected 'File not in scope'), and size the compaction valve from the measured per-iteration growth (0.005 x 16M = 80,000 tokens/segment => L=67 iterations, per-segment counter peak 2.84M = 17.7% of cap). Replayed 200-iteration run: 8.44M real input instead of 23.35M (-64%) with no cap trip.

title: [P1] The recycled-uid recovery (1d1fb4c) fires but does not recover: after its one-shot teardown+bring-up the agent session still cannot reach user@<recycled-uid>.service, so spawn keeps dying at stage rootless-install and the standalone gate's nested regression suite stays at PASS=16 / FAIL=14
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 452 on bunker-mvp with the deployed HEAD 8aa4d8a (the daemon carries the INT-SPAWN-001 fix 1d1fb4c): the standalone gate's nested regression suite (its OWN daemon on 127.0.0.1:29092, isolated ports per the INT-CI-012 fix) still fails spawn at the rootless-install stage, and the NEW recovery path runs and STILL loses. Daemon log /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log, 15:41:13-15:41:16Z, verbatim: (1) 15:41:13.488 INFO 'spawn entering stage' agent_id=regr-alpha stage=rootless-install; (2) 15:41:13.882 WARN 'agent user manager unreachable from the agent session before the rootless install' user=bunker-regr-alpha unit=user@1002.service state='unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success)' linger_entries=6 journal='...docker.service: Failed with result exit-code...'; (3) 15:41:13.937 WARN 'recycled-uid recovery: the unit is ACTIVE but the agent session cannot reach the manager; tearing the foreign manager down and bringing the manager up again' uid=1002; (4) 15:41:14.763 WARN the same unreachable message again; (5) 15:41:14.976 ERROR 'spawn failed ... rootless-install: agent user manager unreachable before the rootless install ... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success); linger entries: 6; journal: <new manager startup lines>; recycled-uid recovery was attempted once (user@1002.service torn down and brought back up) and the agent session still cannot reach the manager'. The same sequence repeated for the next spawn (agent_id=42a1b1e1, uid 1002, 15:41:15.8-15:41:16.8). TIMING: the whole recovery (teardown + bring-up + final probe) fits in ~0.83s (13.937 -> 14.763) and the final probe fails ~30ms after the second WARN - consistent with a bus/manager that is not yet serving the agent session when the final probe runs, but the artifact cannot prove it because the probe's own error text is DISCARDED. DIAGNOSABILITY GAP (fix this first, it is one line): proveUserManagerReachableErr (internal/agent/rootless.go:418) formats '... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; %s; linger entries: %d; journal: %s' from the unit state, the linger count and the journal excerpt - the probe's own error (returned by userSessionRunner, i.e. the actual systemctl/su stderr) is dropped, so every live occurrence names the symptom set but never the cause. Include the probe error in the attribution and in the recovery's final error, then re-run the standalone gate and read the real cause. CONTRAST THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A MISDIAGNOSIS: on the SAME host, minutes earlier, the PRODUCTION daemon (same binary) spawned an agent on a recycled uid 1002 whose previous owner's manager was still ACTIVE - `systemctl show user@1002.service -p ActiveState` = active/SubState running after the destroy - and that spawn completed with NO recovery WARN at all (plain stages rootless-install -> dockerd-start -> session-probe, rc 0, exec rc 0). So the probe CAN succeed against an active foreign manager; it fails in the nested-suite context. Candidate causes worth measuring first: (a) the final probe runs on a su-login session whose XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS point at a runtime dir the recovery just recreated (stale bus inode vs new socket), (b) the bring-up returns before the user manager's bus socket is actually accepting (a bounded connectivity wait, not a fixed budget), (c) linger churn (linger_entries 6, one entry was held for a live agent at that moment) starving the manager start. PASS: (1) the attribution error carries the probe's own stderr; (2) a controlled repro on the demo host (or the nested suite) shows the recovery actually recovering - the second probe succeeds and the spawn completes on a recycled uid in that context; (3) the standalone gate's nested regression suite reports 0 FAIL (its 14 red cells go green); (4) the fix does not weaken the healthy path (no destructive call when the first probe succeeds) and adds at most one bounded wait.

detail:
[P3] MEASURED tick 452 in the standalone gate run on bunker-mvp (/tmp/tick452-standalone.log): the battery printed 'e2e-full-battery.sh: line 1774: [: 0
0: integer expression expected' followed by "  ⚠ changed-spec image count probe: '0

title: [P1] spawn dies at rootless-install with 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' because the readiness gate is a socket-file stat, not a bus handshake: the manager is up (is-active=active, dbus.socket Listening) while the agent session cannot connect
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 453 on bunker-mvp with the INT-SPAWN-002 fix deployed (87aa282 applied to /opt/bunker, rebuilt, installed, bunkerd restarted): the standalone nested suite still reports PASS=16 / FAIL=14 and EVERY red cell is a spawn that dies at stage rootless-install. The new attribution (INT-SPAWN-002 C1) names the real error for the first time, verbatim: session_probe='Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' with unit user@1002.service is-active=active (Result=success) and linger_entries=8. Journal for the same second (16:10:25-16:10:27Z) shows the manager coming up cleanly - 'Starting user@1002.service', 'Listening on dbus.socket', 'systemctl --user set-environment DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus' - then the su session (pam_unix(su-l:session) opened and closed) fails with ENOMEDIUM 0.7s later, the recovery stops the unit, a NEW manager starts, and the SECOND probe fails with the same error. The one-shot recovery therefore runs to completion and the failure reproduces immediately after it. NOT THE MECHANISM (disproved by controlled probes on the production daemon the same tick): (a) same-name uid recycling alone - spawn/destroy/spawn of tick453-alpha reused uid 1002 and succeeded twice with exec OK; (b) an ACTIVE manager for a deleted account - spawn tick453-beta, userdel -rf only (user@1003 is-active=active, logind record gone), spawn tick453-gamma on the recycled uid 1003 succeeded with exec OK. The stale-logind-record WARN of INT-SPAWN-002 did NOT fire during the failing run. LEADING HYPOTHESIS (not yet proven): waitForUserManager only polls os.Stat(<runtimeDir>/bus) - it returns as soon as the socket PATH exists, which is not evidence that the bus accepts a connection; in the failing runs the probe arrives ~0.7s after a fresh manager start and libdbus answers ENOMEDIUM. FIX DIRECTION: replace the stat with a bounded BUS-LEVEL readiness check (repeat the real session-side probe - or an equivalent connect/handshake - inside the existing userManagerWaitTimeout budget, treating 'socket exists but will not answer' as NOT READY rather than as the final attribution), then attribute honestly when the budget is exhausted. Keep the one-shot recovery semantics and the zero-destructive-action healthy path. PASS: (1) the nested suite's spawn cells go green on the demo host (tally PASS=30 / FAIL=0 or, at minimum, the rootless-install failures gone) OR a first-attempt probe that is refused-while-the-manager-is-starting is explicitly retried within the budget and the spawn then succeeds; (2) a unit test proves the readiness loop retries a not-yet-answering socket and still fails bounded and attributed when the manager never answers; (3) the healthy path still probes once with zero destructive calls. EVIDENCE: /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log on bunker-mvp (16:10:25-16:10:28Z), journalctl -u user@1002.service for the same window.

Filing it separately keeps INT-SPAWN-002 (its diagnosability and record-clearing halves landed and are unit-proven) from being silently re-opened and gives the next worker the exact log evidence plus two disproved theories so it does not re-derive them.

title: [P1] `su -` RESETS the session environment, so userSessionEnv's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS never reach the agent session: the probe gets NEITHER variable and systemctl answers 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' - a PERMANENT condition in any daemon not launched by systemd (the standalone gate's nested suite), not the readiness race INT-SPAWN-003 assumed
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 454 on bunker-mvp (78.46.173.180) with the INT-SPAWN-003 fix deployed (a499216 installed to /usr/local/bin/bunker+bunkerd, nested regression suite run standalone on its own ports, log /tmp/tick454-nested.log, daemon log /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log). The nested suite is STILL PASS=16 / FAIL=14 and every red cell is a spawn dying at stage rootless-install. The new readiness wait proves the condition is PERMANENT rather than a late-answering bus: 16:38:09.324Z INFO retry line (first probe refused, session_probe='Failed to connect to bus: No medium found', unit user@1002.service is-active=active), 16:38:39.387Z the FULL-30s-budget exhaustion WARN + one-shot recycled-uid recovery, 16:38:40.167Z the recovery's own readiness wait starts and burns ANOTHER 30s (16:39:10.204Z final attribution, same error). ~60s of probing across a manager teardown+bring-up without a single successful answer. ROOT CAUSE, PROVEN BY CONTROLLED PROBES THIS TICK (all commands run as root on the host): (1) `su -` RESETS THE ENVIRONMENT - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus su - kara -c 'echo XDG=[$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR] DBUS=[$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS]'` prints `XDG=[] DBUS=[]`, so the env userSessionEnv sets on the `su` process (internal/agent/rootless.go userSessionEnv, called by runUserSessionCmd/runRootlessInstallerCmd) is STRIPPED before the probe runs - the file comment claiming the values are 'layered on top of the inherited environment' and 'the installer call uses the SAME construction' is factually wrong for `su -`; (2) the EXACT error text is the no-variable case - `env -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR systemctl --user daemon-reload` on the same host prints verbatim 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'; (3) IN-BAND injection works - `su - kara -c "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus sh -c 'echo \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR'"` prints `/run/user/1002`; (4) the CONTRAST that makes this host-context-dependent: the systemd-launched production daemon on this same host (env carries NEITHER variable) spawns agents successfully, and the host journal records NO pam_systemd 'New session ... of user bunker-<id>' line for the failing su calls (only pam_unix su-l session open/close), so no login stack provides the bus address in that context either - the mechanism behind the contrast (why pam_systemd registers no session for the su child in the non-systemd case) is the ONE thing still unmeasured. FIX DIRECTION: stop relying on the su process environment - build the session environment INSIDE the command the session runs (e.g. `su - <user> -c 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<dir> DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=<dir>/bus systemctl --user daemon-reload'`, or a `env ... sh -c` wrapper) for the probe, the daemon-reload retry AND the rootless installer call, keeping one shared construction so INT-CI-009's 'same env for every user-session command' property becomes TRUE instead of aspirational; add a live-faithful unit test that fails against a runner which sets cmd.Env only. PASS: (1) the nested suite's spawn cells go green on the demo host (the 14 red cells clear; tally PASS=30 / FAIL=0) OR a controlled repro shows the probe succeeding in the non-systemd daemon context; (2) a unit test proves the session command carries the bus address in-band and the probe no longer depends on pam_systemd setting anything; (3) the healthy production path is unchanged (probe succeeds, zero destructive calls, one probe when the bus answers immediately); (4) go build/vet/test/gofmt clean. EVIDENCE: /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log 16:38:08-16:39:13Z on bunker-mvp, the four controlled probes above, /tmp/tick454-nested.log. MECHANISM MEASURED (same tick, two probes on the host, 16:48Z): running the SAME su from a logind session vs from a non-session context flips pam_systemd's behaviour. (A) from the ssh login session that launches the standalone gate: `su - kara -c 'echo XDG=[$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR] DBUS=[$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS]'` -> `XDG=[] DBUS=[]` (no bus address); (B) the production-daemon shape, a transient service outside any logind session: `systemd-run --quiet --wait --pipe --unit=tick454-probe su - kara -c ...` -> `XDG=[/run/user/1001] DBUS=[unix:path=/run/user/1001/bus]`. pam_systemd therefore sets the bus environment for the su session ONLY when the calling process is not already inside a logind session; when the daemon descends from an ssh login session it provides nothing, and because `su -` strips the caller's environment the agent session ends up with NEITHER variable. That is why the production systemd daemon and the CI runner (both services, no logind session) spawn fine while the ssh-launched standalone gate fails 100% - the same binary, the same host, a different launch context. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the session bus environment must be built IN-BAND (inside the command the session runs) and must never depend on pam_systemd or on the su process environment; probe (3) above already proves the in-band form reaches the child.

title: [P1] A spawn that lands on a UID still carrying the previous agent's systemd state hangs 5 minutes, fails `user manager did not start`, and the rollback fails too — leaving an orphan user+home+linger entry that no API surface reports
detail:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-18 on bunker-las-02 (v0.1.4 = HEAD 967c331), reproduced through the daemon's own log trail.
CLIENT VIEW: POST SpawnAgent {"agent_id":"df0918-ttl","ttl":"2m"} -> no response at all for 300s (the client's documented request_timeout) -> socket TimeoutError. With a 330s client timeout the real answer arrives at 5m0.001s: HTTP 500, 154B, {"code":"internal"}. There is no progress signal, no streaming, no way to tell 'slow spawn' from 'dead spawn'.
DAEMON LOG (journalctl -u bunkerd): creating user -> persisted SSH private key -> starting rootless dockerd -> 'resetting user manager runtime' uid=1012 runtime_dir=/run/user/1012 -> 'lazily unmounted stale runtime mount' -> 5 MINUTES OF SILENCE -> 'rolling back: removing user' -> ERROR 'rollback userdel failed' error="context deadline exceeded" -> ERROR 'spawn agent failed' error="install rootless docker for bunker-df0918-ttl: user manager did not start for bunker-df0918-ttl: context deadline exceeded" -> '500 154B in 5m0.001132966s'.
RESIDUE LEFT (the data-loss/blast-radius part): the rollback reuses the already-expired spawn context, so `userdel` fails and the host keeps /etc/passwd uid 1012 bunker-df0918-ttl, /home/bunker-df0918-ttl (36K, partially installed) and a FRESH linger entry /var/lib/systemd/linger/bunker-df0918-ttl. The key /etc/bunkerd/ssh/df0918-ttl WAS removed by the rollback. GetAgent df0918-ttl -> 404 not_found: the daemon has no record of any of it, and neither `bunker list` nor `bunker status` can show or clean it.
HOST STATE THAT CORRELATES: UID 1012 previously belonged to a deleted agent (bunker-59bd09c1) whose user-1012.slice was STILL ACTIVE since 2026-09-14 (3 days; `systemctl is-active user-1012.slice` = active) with no matching /etc/passwd user, 145 lingering bunker-* entries in /var/lib/systemd/linger, stale /run/user/1002..1008 dirs, 5 orphan homes and 4 orphan keys. CONTROL EXPERIMENT: after deleting the residue user+home at the operator level, a new spawn that landed on the SAME UID 1012 succeeded normally in 21.8s ('dockerd ready' -> 'agent registered' -> 'spawned successfully', then destroyed cleanly) — so the host is healthy once the stale per-UID state is gone. Hypothesis for the worker to prove (NOT claimed as established): useradd reuses a freed UID while the old occupant's user-<uid>.slice / linger entry / /run/user/<uid> persist, so the new agent's systemd --user manager cannot start inside the spawn deadline. Consequences operators actually hit: a 5-minute stall on a ticket, litter that accumulates (self-reinforcing: each failed spawn adds another linger entry), and no surface that reports it. This is the failure-mode half of GAP-080 (which measured orphan homes+linger on the demo host but never connected them to spawn failures) and a sibling of DF-BUNKER-18.
FIX DIRECTION: (a) rollback must run on a FRESH context with its own timeout so a failed spawn always cleans up after itself (and retry userdel best-effort; kill the user manager / stop user-<uid>.slice first if userdel hangs); (b) before reusing a UID, reset the per-UID state the daemon already detects as stale (it logs the stale mount but does not stop the stale slice/linger); (c) expose residue counts (orphan users/homes/keys/linger) in `bunker status` and provide a documented prune/reconcile path; (d) return a progress/partial error instead of 5 minutes of silence, or document the 5-minute spawn deadline. PASS: on a host seeded with stale per-UID state, spawn either succeeds or fails FAST (<60s) with an actionable error and leaves ZERO residue (user, home, key, linger); a test reproduces the recycled-UID-with-stale-slice case and asserts cleanup.

title: [P1] docs/integration.md documents ExecAgent as server-streaming but gives no REST recipe — the §2-documented call returns a bare 415 with NO {"code","message"} envelope
detail:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-18 against bunker-las-02 (v0.1.4 = HEAD 967c331) with a stdlib REST client written from docs/integration.md alone (no CLI, no protobuf).
(a) The documented call fails opaquely: POST /bunker.v1.Bunkerd/ExecAgent with Content-Type: application/json (exactly what §2 prescribes) -> HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type, Content-Length: 0, EMPTY body. §2 promises 'Errors carry a JSON {"code","message"} envelope and a real HTTP status', so a doc-following integrator gets neither a hint nor a code. 30+ minutes of the run went into reverse-engineering the surface.
(b) The working shape is connect streaming and is documented NOWHERE: Content-Type: application/connect+json; request body = [flags:1][len:4 BE][json] envelopes; response 200 + Transfer-Encoding: chunked; stdout/stderr arrive as protojson base64 bytes one envelope per write; exitCode only present when non-zero; final frame is a flags=0x02 trailer. `Connect-Protocol-Version: 1` is NOT required (verified).
(c) Both spec-shaped end-of-stream endings are rejected, and both are delivered as HTTP 200 with the error INSIDE the stream: trailing single byte 0x02 -> {"error":{"code":"invalid_argument","message":"protocol error: incomplete envelope: unexpected EOF"}}; trailing [0x02][0x00000000] envelope -> {"error":{"code":"internal","message":"unmarshal end stream message: unexpected end of JSON input"}}. A client that checks only the status code reads these as success with empty output. Only 'no EOS envelope, let Content-Length end the request' works.
Residual of DF-BUNKER-19 (which documented the unary response shapes): the streaming half was never covered.
FIX: add a copy-pasteable streaming example (curl/python) to docs/integration.md §5 + a §2 sentence naming the connect content-type as the streaming exception, AND return a real {"code","message"} envelope for the 415 (or a MediaType error) so the failure is self-explaining. PASS: (1) the doc contains a runnable ExecAgent-over-REST example that returns command output; (2) the wrong content-type produces a JSON envelope naming the expected type; (3) a test asserts the envelope. Evidence: docs/dogfood/2026-09-18-integration.md §4.1-4.3.

title: [P1] ExecAgent corrupts the HTTP response when a command writes to BOTH stdout and stderr - two goroutines call connect's unlocked ServerStream.Send concurrently (0/10 decodable responses on bunker-las-02; the daemon logs 'superfluous response.WriteHeader' at the same second)
detail:
SURFACED BY DF-BUNKER-22's live verification and NOT fixed there (that row touches no exec behavior; this one does).
MEASURED 2026-09-18 against bunker-las-02 (v0.1.4, commit cef10fc) with the stdlib REST client committed in DF-BUNKER-22, exec-only against the pre-existing agent kara-lair (no spawns/destroys): stdout-only 'echo OUT' = 10/10 framing intact; stderr-only 'echo ERR 1>&2' = 10/10; silent 'true' = 5/5; BOTH pipes ('echo OUT; echo ERR 1>&2') = 0/10 decodable. INDEPENDENT FOREMAN REPRO = 3/3 failed, three different failure texts ('truncated envelope: flags=0x31 needs 1628244480 bytes, 102 left'; and twice a body whose raw bytes carry the envelope frames followed by the literal 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' status line).
RAW WIRE (raw socket on the las-02 loopback, ~half the attempts): the status line/header block, a chunk framer and the same envelope bytes appear interleaved and duplicated in one response, e.g. body bytes preceding the status line entirely: '\x00\x00\x00\x00\x15{"stderr":"RVJSCg=="}\x00\x00\x00\x00\x15{"stdout":"T1VUCg=="}HTTP/1.1 200 OK'.
TWO WRITERS ARE PRODUCING ONE RESPONSE.
DAEMON JOURNAL at the same second: 'http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call from github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.(*basicWriter).Write (wrap_writer.go:99)' and the WriteHeader variant (wrap_writer.go:91), 2 lines, bunker-las-02 bunkerd[269333].
CAUSE (strongly indicated, not proven end to end): internal/server/service.go ExecAgent starts ONE goroutine per pipe and each calls connect's ServerStream.Send directly; connect@v1.20.0 protocol_connect.go:809 Send() is unlocked and both goroutines flush through the same http.ResponseWriter. Clients cannot work around it (the corruption is in the byte stream, not in framing the client controls). Documented workaround in docs/integration.md: merge the streams inside the agent ('... 2>&1').
FIX: serialize the stream writes (a mutex around Send, or a single writer goroutine fed by both pipes) so concurrent pipe readers cannot interleave into one response.
PASS: (1) test pins it - a command writing to BOTH pipes produces a decodable stream with both payloads intact over repeated runs; (2) LIVE on bunker-mvp after deploy: a both-pipe command decodes 10/10 with stdout AND stderr present and the exit code faithful, while stdout-only/stderr-only stay 10/10; (3) no behavior change for single-stream commands; (4) AGENTS.md applies (exec-path change): live E2E battery VERIFY-PASS evidence committed.

title: S6 HERMES SHIM: the translated tool surface, CONSTANT in size regardless of how many bunkers exist. The tool list is fixed by the number of verbs; the bunker is an ARGUMENT resolved per call (explicit target > session binding > REFUSAL naming the missing binding, never a global default). Deliberately NO per-bunker registration: with 20 bunkers a per-target design would mean 20 read tools and 200 registrations, and every spawn/destroy would change the tool list. Verbs cover the local parameters, not a reduced set: bunker_read (path, offset, limit, max_bytes -> line-numbered window with total_lines/next_offset), bunker_search (pattern, path, target=content|files, output_mode=content|files_only|count, context, file_glob, limit), bunker_write (whole-file, atomic), bunker_edit (old_string/new_string/replace_all, unique-match refusal naming the count), bunker_patch (unified diff, strict no-fuzz), bunker_apply (atomic multi-file), bunker_exec, bunker_run (detach), bunker_lsp, bunker_lease. Per-session isolation uses the existing BUNKER_HOME relocation keyed by HERMES_SESSION_ID, so concurrent sessions never share a server list, token or key. Capability variance is an ERROR, not a dynamic tool list: a missing verb returns a structured capability_unavailable naming what is absent (toolsd not on agent / no language server / agent_stopped / daemon predates capability reporting) while the verb stays on the surface. Deliverable: the shim in the Hermes agent project, per-session profile wiring, and the binding held as session state (never a tool registration). PASS: (1) every verb works against a real remote tree with output shaped like the local equivalent; (2) CONSTANT-SURFACE proof: spawn one bunker and destroy another, then enumerate the offered tool list - byte-identical before and after, nothing registered or removed; (3) two sessions with different bindings run concurrently with zero cross-writes and zero shared-state reads; (4) unverified calls close as 'unverified' and are never rendered as success; (5) a verb the target lacks returns capability_unavailable with the verb still present; (6) measured per-call verify overhead recorded, not assumed negligible.

title: P2 - md2html.py inline spans rendered as a literal \1 (all PRD HTML output corrupt)
detail: scripts/md2html.py inline() used r"\\1" in its three re.sub replacements. In a Python raw string \\1 is a literal backslash followed by '1', not a group reference, so every <strong>, <em> and <code> span emitted the two characters \1 instead of the matched text. Measured: 216 occurrences in docs/prd/PRD-bunker-remote-editing.html; all bold/emphasis/inline-code content was destroyed while the surrounding prose rendered fine, so it read as a garbled document rather than an obviously broken one. Fixed in the same commit as the PRD rewrite: the three patterns now use \1. Verified by regenerating all six PRDs in coding-hermes-tools + bunker and diffing - the five pre-existing ones differ only by genuine emphasis/code spans that the bug had been silently dropping (PRD-secret-surface-guardian.html: 4 insertions / 2 deletions of real markup). This is a shared skill asset (devops/prd-authoring), not a repo file, so the fix landed in ~/.hermes/skills/devops/prd-authoring/scripts/md2html.py.
reasoning: Every PRD delivered as phone HTML passes through this converter; a silent corruption that drops all emphasis and inline code degrades exactly the dense technical content these docs carry.

title: S8 PER-SESSION TOOL ENABLE/DISABLE + EXECUTION-STATE ISOLATION: a Hermes session must be able to enable and disable its own tools dynamically, and a tool loaded for one session must never reuse another session's state. Measured gap today: `hermes chat -t <toolsets>` is genuinely per-run but ephemeral and start-time-only, while the persistent surface `hermes tools enable|disable` writes ONE global config - agent.disabled_toolsets and plugins.disabled in a single config.yaml read by every session on the box. So enabling a tool for one session currently toggles a global: the same shared-mutable-pointer shape as the active_server routing bug. Design rule (Rule B of the PRD): a session's ENABLED SET is session state, never global config - enabling a verb for this session writes one row (this session's own) and re-projects the tool list for this session only. Pair it with the sharing rule: registration metadata (name, JSON schema, description) is SHARED and immutable, while EXECUTION state (MCP client connection, plugin instance, LSP session, caches, lease handles, open file handles) is PER SESSION and never pooled - a pooled stateful client handed from session A to B would leak subscriptions, working directory, half-open files, cached reads and LSP document state. Mechanically the session tool list is: constant catalog -> this session's enabled row -> per-session projection into the system prompt -> dispatch against THIS session's enabled set (an unenabled verb refuses as tool_not_enabled_in_session, distinct from capability_unavailable) -> any instance created is keyed (session_id, tool) and released at session end. NO per-session re-registration is required, and no per-bunker registration either. PASS: (1) SESSION ISOLATION: two concurrent sessions; A disables a tool while B keeps it, then both toggle a different tool in the same minute - each session's offered list matches only its own choices, B is unaffected both ways, and the global config's disabled_toolsets / plugins.disabled are byte-identical before and after; (2) NO-STATE-REUSE: A loads a stateful tool and leaves it warm (cached read / open path / LSP document), then B loads the same tool and gets a fresh instance with no A-derived state - proved by asserting B's instance does not contain A's distinguishable artifact; (3) DYNAMIC: a mid-session enable/disable takes effect for that session on its next turn without a restart and without touching another session; (4) NO-STRANDING: killing a session holding per-session state reclaims its instances instead of stranding them, and a later session's footprint is unaffected; (5) the refusal for an unenabled verb is distinct from the refusal for an unsupported one; (6) a documented memory budget: per-session state scales with CONCURRENTLY ACTIVE sessions, not total starts.
detail: PRD S8, Rule B. The user's requirement is that tool enable/disable be session-local and that loaded tool state never be reused across sessions; today the persistent surface is global config, so a session toggling a tool changes what every other session is offered. This is the tools-side twin of the routing bug GAP-093 fixes.

title: HERMES-SIDE SUPPORT GAP (audit result 2026-09-20): of everything this PRD needs from Hermes, only ONE capability is actually missing, and the audit that found that is now recorded in the PRD section 'What Hermes already supports'. ALREADY TRUE (verified live, do not rebuild): MCP instances are per-session - 17 `toolsd mcp` processes under 15 distinct parents (Hermes session processes + cron.scheduler), so there is no shared MCP client state to leak; `toolsd` is already registered as an MCP server (config.yaml:1060, enabled:true); `hermes chat -t <toolsets>` projects toolsets per run; `hermes hooks` (shell + outbound webhook, first-use consent allowlist) can gate a tool call and is a viable interim enforcement point. THE GAP: `hermes tools enable|disable` writes ONE global config (agent.disabled_toolsets, plugins.disabled) that every session on the box reads, so a session toggling a tool changes what every other session is offered - the tools-side twin of the active_server routing bug. Also note: `hermes profile use` sets a STICKY DEFAULT, not a per-session pick, so profiles exist but there is no session-keyed resolution today. Deliverable: (1) a session-scoped enabled set resolved per session, with a mid-session enable/disable that re-projects only that session's tool list; (2) profile resolution keyed by session id (HERMES_SESSION_ID already exists) instead of a sticky global; (3) a PINNING TEST that asserts MCP instances remain per-session and are not silently pooled by a future refactor - the current isolation is real but unprotected by any test. PASS: (1) session A disabling a tool leaves session B's list and the global config byte-identical; (2) mid-session toggle takes effect for that session on the next turn with no restart; (3) the pinning test fails if MCP clients are made shared/pooled; (4) an unenabled verb refuses as tool_not_enabled_in_session, distinct from capability_unavailable; (5) the hooks interim is documented so it can be used before the native path lands.

title: MOUNT LIFECYCLE: proper cleanup, preflight, and a mountpoint a non-root user can actually use. MEASURED DEFECTS TODAY (verified 2026-09-20): (a) DEFAULT MOUNTPOINT IS UNUSABLE for a normal operator - mount.go:216 does os.MkdirAll(mountPoint, 0755) with a default of /mnt/bunker/<agent-id>, but /mnt here is root:root 0755 and /mnt/bunker does not exist, so the default path fails for any non-root user (the residual already noted under DF-BUNKER-14); (b) NO UNMOUNT PATH AT ALL - the command ends by PRINTING 'Unmount with: fusermount -u <path>' (mount.go:311) and there is no `bunker umount`, so cleanup is a manual shell incantation the operator must remember; (c) NO PREFLIGHT - the mount attempts without first establishing that the remote path EXISTS and is a DIRECTORY, so a dead/re-created agent (empty home) or a typo'd --path yields a mounted EMPTY tree that looks successful, which is precisely the 'writing to a non-existent thing' failure: an editor pointed at a successful-looking but empty mount writes into a fresh empty tree; (d) NO STALE-HANDLING - an interrupted mountpoint (dead FUSE session after a crashed sshfs or a killed network) is not detected, so the next attempt hits 'mountpoint is not empty' and the operator must clear it by hand. DELIVERABLE: (1) mountpoint policy - default under a USER-WRITABLE per-session root (e.g. $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bunker/<agent-id> or ~/.bunker/mnt/<agent-id>), never a root-owned /mnt path, with the override honoured; (2) `bunker umount <agent-id|mountpoint>` that is idempotent (already-unmounted = success), clears a dead mountpoint via lazy unmount when needed, and reports what it did; (3) mount-time PREFLIGHT that verifies the remote path exists and is a directory BEFORE mounting and REFUSES with a named cause otherwise, so an empty tree can never be silently mounted; (4) stale/dirty mountpoint detection with an explicit recover path, and a clear refusal naming the holder when the mountpoint is live and in use; (5) a `bunker mount --json`/status surface listing live mounts (agent, mountpoint, remote path, pid) so cleanup is observable rather than remembered; (6) teardown on daemon/destroy of the agent - destroying an agent must not leave a dangling local mountpoint. PASS: (1) a non-root operator mounts with the default path and it succeeds (no root, no pre-created dir); (2) umount is idempotent and clears a dead mountpoint (proved by killing sshfs and re-running); (3) mounting an agent whose remote path does not exist REFUSES with a named cause and mounts nothing; (4) mounting an agent whose home is empty REFUSES (the empty-tree trap) rather than succeeding; (5) mount --json lists live mounts and a destroyed agent leaves none; (6) no mountpoint is left behind after any failure path; (7) battery VERIFY-PASS if any ssh/exec surface changed.
detail: PRD Path B / S9 slice 1 - the build order the review set: sshfs first. Owns the exact hazards called out in review: cleanup, and never writing into a non-existent path.
reasoning: PRD S9. Measured today: default mountpoint /mnt/bunker/<id> is root-owned so non-root operators cannot use it; there is no umount command, only a printed hint; and nothing verifies the remote path exists, so an empty or wrong tree mounts looking successful.

title: MOUNT NAMESPACE + WORKSPACE RESOLUTION: make the mount know WHICH project tree it is mounting, and validate it. TODAY: mount replays the daemon-stored sshfs command (sshHostFromMount) and swaps the mountpoint; it never resolves or validates the remote PATH as a workspace, so 'which tree' is whatever the daemon happened to store. There is no notion of a workspace, no way to mount a repo inside the agent's home rather than the whole home, and no check that the resolved workspace belongs to the namespace/project the session thinks it is working in. INTERPRETATION (say if this is wrong): 'namespace' = the fleet namespace/project owning the agent, 'workspace' = the tree inside it (the repo), and 'handle correctly' = resolve and validate both before mounting, and record them in the session binding so a session cannot mount one project's tree while believing it is another's. DELIVERABLE: (1) explicit resolution chain server -> agent -> remote path (home by default, --path for a subdirectory such as the repo root, with ~ expansion), all validated to exist and be a directory before use (shared with GAP-103's preflight, same helper); (2) a workspace identity check - the resolved path must carry the expected marker (e.g. the expected git remote or a workspace marker file) or the mount REFUSES naming the mismatch, so mounting the wrong tree is detectable rather than silent; (3) the resolved (server, agent, remote path, namespace) recorded in the session binding and echoed by `bunker mount --json`, so the session knows which project it is in; (4) per-session mountpoints so two sessions on one agent never share a mount path (they may share the TREE, which is correct and guarded by leases - never the mountpoint); (5) docs updated to state plainly what a mount can and cannot guarantee (it cannot enforce binding; concurrent writes are guarded by the per-tree lease registry, CHT-052). PASS: (1) mounting a subdirectory repo works and the mountpoint shows exactly that tree, not the whole home; (2) mounting with a --path that does not exist refuses with a named cause; (3) the workspace identity check refuses when the resolved tree is not the expected project (proved by pointing at another agent's home); (4) two sessions mounting the same agent get DISTINCT mountpoints and see each other's writes through the FS; (5) `bunker mount --json` reports the resolved workspace and namespace; (6) battery VERIFY-PASS if any ssh surface changed.
detail: PRD Path B / S9 slice 2 - namespace + workspace resolution, the review's second call-out.
reasoning: PRD S9. The mount replays the daemon-stored sshfs command and never resolves or validates a workspace, so 'which tree' is whatever the daemon stored and the wrong tree is indistinguishable from the right one.

title: MOUNT FIDELITY + DO-NOT-BUILD GUARD (the 'both ways' groundwork): prove the mount is as good as local for editing, and make the one thing a mount is bad at (local builds) impossible rather than merely discouraged. DELIVERABLE: (1) FIDELITY EVIDENCE - with a real agent mounted, run the local editing tools against the mountpoint and diff every result against a local checkout of the same commit: read_file on a line window (offset/limit + line numbers), patch on a known edit, search_files on a pattern across all three output modes, git diff and git log. Every divergence is written down as a documented mount limitation, not left implicit; (2) DO-NOT-BUILD GUARD - a build/test inside a mounted tree is REFUSED with a message naming `bunker build`: a marker file written at the mountpoint root by mount (e.g. .bunker-mount) plus a wrapper/hook that detects it and refuses, because a naive local `make` over SFTP would both waste the local CPU this design exists to save and run pathologically slowly. The guard must be loud, not silent, and must not break legitimate remote builds; (3) BOTH-WAYS DOC - one page stating when to use the mount (read, grep, diff, small edits, git inspection - highest fidelity because it IS a filesystem) vs the verb layer (writes that must be targeted, attributed and refuse-on-unbound) vs both (builds, always remote). PASS: (1) the fidelity matrix is recorded with raw command/output pairs and any divergence named; (2) a local build inside the mount is refused with a message naming the remote path to use, proved by the refusal firing rather than by a long local build; (3) a legitimate remote build through bunker build still works end-to-end with the guard installed; (4) killing the SSH transport mid-edit yields a bounded, named failure (never an indefinitely hanging tool), no partial write, and one-command recovery; (5) the both-ways doc is linked from README and the PRD.
detail: PRD Path B / S9 slice 3 - fidelity evidence plus the do-not-build guard; closes the mount half of the line.
reasoning: PRD S9 + proofs 17-19. A mount is the highest-fidelity path but the worst possible place to run a build; the guard is what makes the one-mode split (mount for edits, remote for builds) safe rather than aspirational.

title: DYNAMIC PER-INSTANCE TARGETING (the 'new dynamic per bunker instance tools' half): make 'which bunker' a runtime value a session can discover, switch and hold, WITHOUT the tool list growing with the fleet. THE TENSION, RESOLVED EXPLICITLY: an earlier review said do not present 20 read tools for 20 bunkers; a later review asked for dynamic per-bunker-instance tools. Both are satisfied by keeping the CATALOG constant and making the INSTANCE SET dynamic: the tools stay fixed in shape with the target as an argument, while the set of instances a session may target is discovered at runtime and can change mid-session. What is dynamic is the instance REGISTRY and the session BINDING, never the tool catalog. DELIVERABLE: (1) instance discovery - enumerate the reachable bunker instances for this session (from the session profile's server list + the fleet inventory), with liveness and a one-line summary per instance, returned as DATA; (2) session binding - bind/unbind/switch the session's current target at runtime (explicit target wins per call; the binding is the default for that session only); (3) an instance-aware call path so ANY verb can be aimed at any bound instance without a new tool being registered - including a mount-backed mode and a verb-backed mode for the same instance, so both delivery paths reach the same tree; (4) refusal semantics - an unbound session refuses (GAP-093), an unknown instance refuses naming it, and a dead instance refuses as unreachable rather than silently retargeting; (5) no per-instance registration, no restart to pick up a new instance, and no global mutable current-server anywhere on the path. PASS: (1) with three instances known, a session switches between them mid-life and every verb follows the switch with zero cross-writes (proved against two real servers); (2) the offered tool list is byte-identical before and after an instance is added or removed (the constant-catalog proof, restated for instances); (3) the same tree is reachable in BOTH modes (mount-backed and verb-backed) and an edit made through one is visible through the other; (4) an unbound or unknown-instance call refuses with a distinct named cause and touches nothing; (5) two sessions bound to different instances run concurrently with zero interference; (6) discovery output is data (parseable), including explicitly 'unreachable' instances rather than omitting them.
detail: PRD S6/S8 extension - the dynamic-instance half. Resolves the earlier tension explicitly: constant catalog, dynamic instance set.
reasoning: PRD. Delivers 'dynamic per bunker instance tools' without the 20-bunkers-20-read-tools failure mode: what varies per session is the instance registry and the binding, never the verb catalog.

title: MOUNT DURABILITY: no phantom space, no silent disappearance, auto-recovery. Spec of record: docs/prd/SPEC-sshfs-mount-durability.md. MEASURED GAP TODAY (verified 2026-09-20 against internal/cli/mount.go): the mount passes ONLY StrictHostKeyChecking / UserKnownHostsFile / IdentitiesOnly - it passes NONE of the durability options sshfs supports (-o reconnect, -o auto_unmount, ServerAliveInterval/CountMax, ConnectTimeout, dir_cache), even though every OTHER ssh path in this repo (cp, ssh, deploy, session_probe, service) carries -o ConnectTimeout=10. Consequence: a transport blip is permanent, a dropped link leaves stale cached entries so a write appears to succeed into a kernel buffer and is lost (the PHANTOM SPACE), a crashed sshfs strands the mountpoint and blocks the next mount with 'not empty', and nothing detects any of it. DELIVERABLE per the spec: (1) a client-constructed durability option set - reconnect, ServerAliveInterval=15 / ServerAliveCountMax=3, ConnectTimeout=10, auto_unmount, dir_cache=no for the editing profile, idmap=user - added explicitly and asserted present by test, NOT inherited from the daemon-stored command string; (2) a HEALTH PREDICATE with a hard timeout that stats a known marker path and compares its captured content, returning three distinct verdicts - healthy / unreachable (transport dead) / stale (tree is not the one mounted) - because unreachable and stale demand DIFFERENT recovery; (3) WRITE-TIME GUARD: no write is reported successful without a health probe or read-back, and a failed probe REFUSES the write with a named cause (mount_unreachable / mount_stale) instead of attempting and losing it, so the operator is never told an edit landed when it did not; (4) BOUNDED IDEMPOTENT RECOVERY with an explicit policy: unreachable -> wait out the reconnect window then remount ONCE; stale -> NEVER auto-remount (may hold unflushed writes), require an explicit --recover; stranded mountpoint -> clear (normal then lazy) and remount once; busy mountpoint -> never touch, report the holder by pid. The rule that keeps it safe: recovery may RE-ESTABLISH a mount, never RE-TARGET one, and running it twice leaves the same state as running it once; (5) CLEANUP THAT CANNOT BE FORGOTTEN: idempotent `bunker umount`, `bunker mount status`/--json listing every live mount as data (agent, mountpoint, remote path, namespace, pid, health, age), teardown hooks on agent destroy / session end / daemon shutdown, and an orphan sweep for mounts whose owning pid is gone (the mount-side twin of GAP-070's registry reconciliation); (6) state in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bunker/mounts.json - per user, per boot, never a global registry. PASS (each independently checkable): (1) PHANTOM proof - drop the transport mid-session, attempt a write: refused within <=45s as mount_unreachable, no success reported, no partial file on either side; (2) RECONNECT proof - blip <15s and restore: mount recovers with NO operator action and the next read is correct rather than a cached stale entry; (3) STALE proof - destroy and re-create the agent under the same name: reported STALE (not healthy, not unreachable), writes refused, no auto-remount without --recover; (4) STRANDED proof - kill -9 sshfs, mount again: the stale mountpoint is cleared automatically, no manual fusermount; (5) IDEMPOTENCE proof - run recovery twice, state identical (one mount, one registry row); (6) CLEANUP proof - destroy the agent: ZERO local mountpoints remain and mount status lists none; (7) HANG-BOUNDED proof - with the peer firewalled, stat the mountpoint returns a named error within the bounded window, never blocking indefinitely; (8) BUSY proof - request unmount with a live consumer: refused naming the holder pid, live mount undisturbed; (9) ANTI-LYING proof - no success reported without a prior successful probe or read-back.
