title: PLUS ULTRA - MOUNT TEST + REGRESSION HARNESS: the mount chain (GAP-103 lifecycle/cleanup, GAP-107 durability, GAP-104 namespace/workspace, GAP-105 fidelity+guard) currently has NO way to be regression-tested, because every one of its failure modes is a TRANSPORT condition (drop, blip, strand, hang, identity change) rather than an input the unit tests can hand it. Deliverable: a deterministic mount harness that can inject each failure without a real network outage, so the chain is testable in CI and re-verifiable after any refactor. (1) a FAKE SSHFS/SSH double - a stub binary on PATH that speaks the same argv/stdio contract, can be told to succeed, fail permanently, fail transiently then recover, hang, or die mid-write, and can be told to change what it serves (for the stale case). Mirrors the existing real-seam probe recipe used for GAP-079/GAP-084 retry work; (2) FAULT INJECTION at the transport boundary, driven by an env knob, so each of the six spec failure modes is reachable from a test: partial write then death (phantom), permanent drop, transient blip then recovery, stranded mountpoint (process gone, dir remains), elapsed-time hang, and identity swap; (3) a mount STATE assertion helper that reads the registry ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bunker/mounts.json) and asserts the health verdict, so tests assert the three-verdict predicate (healthy/unreachable/stale) rather than stdout; (4) a REGRESSION SUITE wired into `go test ./...` (no root, no real host, hermetic) covering every acceptance criterion of GAP-103/-104/-105/-107 that CAN be tested without a live host, and an explicit named list of the criteria that REQUIRE a live host (deferred to the -LIVE row) so coverage is never implied by omission; (5) a documented LIVE matrix for the remaining proofs, runnable as one script against a real agent on a CI-idle window. PASS: (1) the suite reproduces phantom-write loss, permanent-drop refusal, blip-recovery, strand-recovery, hang-boundedness and identity-swap as six hermetic tests, each RED on the pre-fix code and GREEN after; (2) the suite runs in CI with no root, no network and no real sshfs; (3) mutation check: reverting any single durability option, the health probe, or the write guard makes its test fail - proving the tests are load-bearing rather than decorative; (4) the live-required list is explicit and each entry names its owning -LIVE row; (5) `go test ./... -count=1` stays green and adds no measurable wall-clock regression to the existing suite.

title: PLUS ULTRA - MULTI-BUNKER CAPACITY: 'so we can deploy any number of bunkers and have a lot more capacity'. The goal is N bunkers used concurrently by N sessions with no cross-talk and no per-bunker tool growth. Deliverable: (1) a SCALE PROOF - drive K concurrent sessions against M bunkers (start K,M = 4,2 then raise) doing real edits through both delivery paths, and report throughput, per-session latency, failure count and cross-write count (must be zero). title: PLUS ULTRA - REMOTE CODING EXPERIENCE: make the remote experience not merely functional but equal to local, measured end-to-end on a real project rather than on synthetic edits. This is the row that answers 'is it actually as good as local' with evidence. Deliverable: a scripted end-to-end exercise on a REAL repo (use bunker itself or a small Go project) performed ENTIRELY against a remote bunker, covering the operations a coding session actually performs: (1) orient - list/search the tree, read files in windows, read a large file with continuation; (2) understand - symbol definition/references via lsp, git log/blame/diff for history; (3) edit - a multi-file change through apply, a targeted change through edit, a diff through patch, each with its refusal paths exercised; (4) verify - build and test remotely, capture failures and iterate at least one RED-to-GREEN cycle; (5) collaborate - two concurrent sessions on the same tree, one refused cleanly by the lease; (6) preserve - commit, and prove the local box never held a copy of the tree. Measure and publish per-operation latency alongside the local equivalent, and record every point where the remote experience DIVERGES from local as a named limitation. PASS: (1) the full exercise completes against a real remote tree with the RED-to-GREEN cycle actually happening; (2) every operation's latency is measured against its local equivalent and published, including any bad ratio; (3) the divergence list is explicit and each entry is either fixed or accepted with a reason; (4) 'no local copy' is proven by the local box holding no clone/mount after the exercise; (5) the concurrent-session step shows the lease refusal firing rather than an interleaved write.

title: PLUS ULTRA - REMOTE VERB TEST + REGRESSION: the verb layer (GAP-093 binding, GAP-094 bodies, GAP-097 shim, GAP-106 instances) needs the same test discipline as the mount chain, and for the same reason: its defining behaviours are refusals and boundary conditions, which unit tests only cover if they are built to. Deliverable: (1) a PARITY HARNESS that runs the same arguments through the local tool and the remote verb on the same content and diffs the results - the executable form of acceptance criterion 1 of SPEC-bunker-native-file-tools, so parity is a test rather than an audit; (2) CONFINEMENT TEST MATRIX covering `..` traversal, absolute paths, symlinks pointing outside the root, and a workspace root that is itself a symlink - each must fail ErrOutsideRoot with NOTHING written, proven by a post-condition check on the tree; (3) REFUSAL SUITE asserting the distinct verdicts are actually distinct: no_workspace_bound vs namespace_unknown vs workspace_invalid vs capability_unavailable vs tool_not_enabled_in_session vs lease_conflict - six named causes, six distinct outcomes, because collapsing any two makes the surface lie about why it refused; (4) ATOMICITY TESTS for apply - a failure on file N of M leaves EVERY file byte-identical, proven by hashing the tree before and after; (5) a hermetic FAKE AGENT double so the whole suite runs in CI with no real bunker, plus `go test ./...` integration. PASS: (1) the parity harness reports zero unexplained divergences and the two documented ones are asserted as expected divergences rather than tolerated; (2) every confinement case refuses AND leaves the tree byte-identical (hash-verified); (3) all six refusal verdicts are produced by their own trigger and are distinguishable in the result; (4) apply atomicity holds under injected failure at every file boundary, not just the first; (5) mutation check: removing the confinement check, a refusal cause, or the atomicity rollback makes its test fail; (6) the suite is hermetic and runs in CI (no root, no network, no real agent).
detail: Plus-ultra criterion 4 applied to the verb layer: its defining behaviours are refusals and boundaries, so they are only covered if tests are built for them. Depends on GAP-097 (the shim) so the parity harness compares the real surface.

title: MOUNT LIVE PROOF (carries the mount chain's host-dependent criteria): the code for GAP-103/-107 is landed and unit-tested, but every DURABILITY criterion is a TRANSPORT condition that cannot be unit-tested - it needs a real agent and a controllable network. Run on a CI-idle window against a real agent, and produce raw evidence for each: (1) PHANTOM - with the mount live, drop the transport (kill the agent's sshd or firewall the host), then attempt a write: it must be REFUSED within <=45s with a named cause, no success reported and no partial file on either side; (2) RECONNECT - blip the transport <15s and restore: the mount recovers with NO operator action and the next read returns current data, not a cached stale entry; (3) EMPTY TREE - mount an agent whose home is empty and, separately, a --path that does not exist: both must REFUSE before mounting with nothing created at the mountpoint; (4) STRANDED - kill -9 the sshfs process, then mount again: the stale mountpoint is cleared automatically with no manual fusermount; (5) CLEANUP - destroy the agent: ZERO local mountpoints remain; (6) HANG-BOUNDED - with the peer firewalled, stat the mountpoint: a named error within the bounded window, never an indefinite block; (7) IDEMPOTENCE - run the recovery/umount path twice: state is identical. PASS requires the raw command/output for each of the seven, run in one session, with the mountpoint/agent left clean. NOTE: item (2) requires -o reconnect to actually be honoured by the deployed sshfs version; if a blip kills the mount anyway, that is a FINDING to record rather than a failure to hide.

title: [P1] Agent-service Metrics RPC enforces no per-agent scoping and no existence check — a spawned agent's sub-key can read ANY agent's metrics, and any caller gets a fabricated 'running' record for a never-spawned id
detail: Found by the 2026-09-19 durability run (scratch HEAD e344088 daemon, jwt_secret set so spawn mints sub-keys). Evidence (raw curl, Bunkerd REST :18093): (a) dfdf-a's sub-key POST bunker.v1.Agent/Metrics {"agentId":"dfdf-b"} returned dfdf-b's status+memoryUsedBytes (21.7 GB) — cross-agent read, no 403; (b) the SAME sub-key asking for "kara-lair" (an id that does not exist on this daemon) got {"agentId":"kara-lair","status":"running","memoryUsedBytes":<host value>} — no clamp, no existence check; (c) MASTER token asking for "no-such-agent-xyz" got the same fabricated running record; (d) contrast Agent/Heartbeat on a foreign id → 404 not_found (correct), Agent/GetInfo on a foreign id → clamped to own agent (correct), Bunkerd service with sub-key → 401 (correct). The CLI path (bunker.v1.Bunkerd/AgentMetrics) does check existence, so only the Agent-service surface is affected. Audit shows the calls attributed correctly, so the leak is queryable in the trail. Fix direction: in the agentService Metrics handler apply the same scoping as GetInfo (sub-key → own agent only, 403/404 otherwise) and return not_found for unknown ids instead of host-fallback data with status:running; if host-fallback is intended for masters, gate it behind an explicit request flag and never fabricate status:running for a nonexistent agent. Pass criteria: sub-key Metrics on a foreign id → 403/404; Metrics on a never-spawned id → not_found (any caller); unit tests cover all three probe shapes above.

title: [P1] Audit hash chain breaks on EVERY daemon restart — first post-restart record carries empty prev_hash and `bunker audit verify` reports 'tamper detected' on an untampered log
detail: Found by the 2026-09-19 durability run: scratch daemon restarted (plain restart, then again after kill -9); record 4 of /tmp/df0919/audit.log (first record of the second process) has prev_hash:"" while record 3 (last of the first process) has a normal hash. `bunker audit verify` → 'tamper detected at record 4 / record 4: prev_hash does not chain (tampered)'. Root cause: internal/audit/audit.go keeps lastHash only in memory; rotation keeps the chain via a seal record, but newAuditLog never recovers the chain head from the existing file's tail. Consequence: the tamper-evidence control false-positives on every legitimate restart (systemd restart, deploy, crash) — verify output becomes noise, which trains operators to ignore real tamper reports. Fix direction: at AuditLog open, read the log tail (and rotated segments if verify spans them) to re-seed lastHash; if a seal record is present use the sealed head. Pass criteria: restart a daemon twice against an existing audit.log (one graceful, one SIGKILL), append records, `audit verify` → OK; add a regression test that opens an existing chained log, appends, and verifies.

title: [P2] config.example.yaml reconciliation comment omits the adopt precondition — 'adopt: re-registered + exact port reservation restored' silently destroys any orphan without readable /home/bunker-<id>/.bunker/ports
detail: 2026-09-19 run: with mode: adopt explicitly set (confirmed in the startup log line), a synthetic orphan (useradd bunker-dforph-a1, no .bunker/ports) was WARNed ('adopt failed … no readable port metadata') and DESTROYED at startup — destroyed:1, adopted:0. The code path (internal/agent/reconcile.go, 'Adoption of the rest requires readable, valid, free port metadata') is fail-closed by design; only the config.example.yaml comment (lines ~105-111) understates it, so an operator expecting bare users to be adopted gets them destroyed instead. Fix direction: extend the comment: adopt applies ONLY to orphans carrying readable in-pool port metadata; anything else is destroyed in both modes (log line names the reason). Pass criteria: the comment states the metadata precondition and the destroy fallback.

detail: 2026-09-19 re-confirmation at HEAD e344088: `bunker exec --config X dfdf-a -- cmd` → 'exec takes no flags before <agent-id>', while the same global flag before the verb works for spawn/list/status/mount/etc. Every dogfood run since 09-16 trips on this at least once (this run: twice).
